card: This pull request brings Windows support to Bitcoin Core's IPC subsystem and updates libmultiprocess. It replaces POSIX-only process spawning and socket handling with Windows equivalents such as named pipes, WSADuplicateSocket, and overlapped I/O, allowing multiprocess binaries to build and run on Windows. The changes also adapt the Python test runner for Windows AF_UNIX sockets and fix the Windows wrapper binary so it accurately tracks child exit statuses. This resolves long-standing libmultiprocess issues (#53, #114) and enables multiprocess Bitcoin on Windows (#10102).
changed_since_previous: Incorporated latest upstream libmultiprocess commits, fixed the Windows ExecVp wrapper to wait on child exit codes via _cwait, enabled tool_bitcoin and interface_gui tests on Windows, added Windows AF_UNIX asyncio workarounds to the Python test framework, and resolved several MinGW/MSVC build and runtime issues.

enables: Windows multiprocess node and GUI binaries (#10102, #28722)

evidence: PR description notes it resolves libmultiprocess issues #53 and #114 as part of the broader process separation project (#28722).

Commit 4957ab2189 fixes Windows wrapper execution: 'Switch from _execvp to _spawnvp(_P_NOWAIT) + _cwait so bitcoin.exe waits for the child process to finish and forwards its exit code. Previously _execvp would exit the parent as soon as the child started, making it impossible for anything waiting on bitcoin.exe (such as a test framework) to track whether the child succeeded or failed.'
problem: IPC and multiprocess features cannot build or run on Windows because libmultiprocess and Core process management primitives rely on POSIX APIs (fork, execvp, Unix domain sockets), preventing Windows users and developers from testing or using the multiprocess node architecture.

risk.why: Mistakes in Windows process spawning, pipe I/O, or socket error mappings could cause hangs, unhandled crashes on child startup, or broken CLI/wrapper execution on Windows.

scope_notes: Contains a substantial subtree update for src/ipc/libmultiprocess (+2592/-839 across 99 files) and temporarily skips subtree link linting while draft changes are inlined. It also refactors all Windows executable resource (.rc) generation into a single CMake helper template.
summary: This pull request implements Windows support for Bitcoin Core's IPC subsystem and updates the libmultiprocess subtree. It replaces POSIX-only process spawning and socket primitives with Windows equivalents (named pipes, WSADuplicateSocket, overlapped I/O, and _cwait process tracking), consolidates Windows executable manifest and resource handling via CMake, and enables IPC targets in MinGW and MSVC CI builds. It also adds Windows AF_UNIX emulation in the Python functional test framework to allow running IPC test suites.
